newsitem.title: CANADA: Jordan switches to 50,000 T Canadian wheat-trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan switches to 50,000 T Canadian wheat-trade.

text.p: Jordan overnight switched its optional-origin wheat purchase to 50,000 tonnes Canadian wheat from U.S. hard red winter wheat for delivery Aug 15-Oct 15, grain trade sources said.
Jordan's tender Wednesday called for two optional-origin cargoes of 50,000 tonnes each for two delivery periods: Aug 15-Sept 15 and Sept 15-Oct 15, one source said.
U.S. exporters bid at just under US$172.00 a tonne, cost, insurance and freight with federal GSM 102 financing.
Canadian Wheat Board countered with a bid of US$169.00 CIF Jordan, one source said.
Another source placed the CWB's bid closer to US$171.00 CIF Jordan or US$155 to US$156 FOB St. Lawrence River.
"Fifty thousand tonnes were switched and the balance might be switched," the source said.
CWB spokesman Jim Pietryk would neither confirm nor deny the trade talk.
